Agreement no. PH-13838

attachments.name: crowd_plan.txt
attachments.text:
CROWD MANAGEMENT PLAN
Harbour Harriers City Race 7K, Saturday 8 May 2027
Applicant: Harbour Harriers Athletic Club
Prepared by Ruth Abernathy, Event Coordinator
Issue: 1.0

1. Attendance
We expect 2600 people in total at the event, including 1800 runners. We allow for 800 spectators.

2. Spectator areas
We anticipate that spectators will gather naturally around the start and finish, as well as at convenient points along the course, creating an enjoyable atmosphere for all participants. Signage will be placed around the site to help visitors find their way, and refreshments will be on sale close to the finish.

Families are welcome, and there is usually a friendly atmosphere at the finish. Local shops have been supportive, and some stay open for the day. The prize-giving takes place at the end, and there is often a queue for tea.

3. Start procedure
All entrants will assemble in the start area shortly before 09:00 and will start together following a short welcome and warm-up led by a local sports personality, which has always proved popular in previous years.

4. Stewarding
52 stewards in high-visibility tabards, led by 6 supervisors, are allocated by position on the attached rota. That is around one steward for every 50 people expected. All attend a briefing at the site one hour before the start.

5. Exit and dispersal
Following the race, participants and their families are welcome to stay and enjoy the prize-giving and refreshments before making their own way home at their leisure. There are good public transport links nearby.

6. Event control
The event controller, Ruth Abernathy, sits at the control point with radio contact to all supervisors and can hold a start, stop the race or use the public address to move people. A supervisor reports to the controller if any pen or viewing area appears to be filling beyond its marked capacity.

attachments.name: medical_plan.txt
attachments.text:
Medical cover for the Harbour Harriers City Race 7K, Saturday 8 May 2027

From Ruth Abernathy, Event Coordinator, Harbour Harriers Athletic Club

The race is a 7K with 1800 runners and starts at 09:00. On-site ambulance cover is set out in the attached paperwork from St. Luke Ambulance Brigade.

First aid
We'll have 3 first aid posts, at the start, the finish and halfway, with 12 trained first aiders between them, so nobody on the course is more than about a kilometre and a half from help. We also have two first aiders on bikes, carrying defibrillators.

In recent years the last runner has usually finished well inside the time limit, and past incidents have been limited to a few blisters and one twisted ankle. A number of members have first aid certificates from work and are glad to be there in a general helping role.

Heat, cold and water
There's water every 2.5 km. We look at the forecast two days before and again two hours before. Over 28 degrees we start earlier or cut the course, and over 32 degrees we call it off. If it's cold or wet, we have foil blankets and a warm tent at the finish.

If someone needs hospital
The nearest emergency department is at Harbourside Medical Centre, 10 km from the finish. We've walked the route out from the pick-up point at the top of Dyer Street with the first aiders, and we've told the hospital the date and how many are coming.

Staying in touch
Everyone at a post and both bike first aiders has a radio on our medical channel, with phones as backup. Calls for an ambulance go through our medical lead, who tells the crew which barrier to come to.

Who's responsible
Our medical lead is Carl Jensen, a registered paramedic, who'll be there from an hour before the start until the last runner is in and has the final word on pulling any runner out.

attachments.name: race_plan.txt
attachments.text:
RACE PLAN
Harbour Harriers City Race 7K | Saturday 8 May 2027
Organiser: Harbour Harriers Athletic Club
Race director: Ruth Abernathy
Reference: AG-26719

Overview
The Harbour Harriers City Race 7K is a 7K race of 7 km for 1800 entrants, based in the Kingsway Gardens area of Port Halden. The start is at 09:00 and the course closes at 10:30.

Course
The course runs in order along Dyer Street, Tanner Street, Bell Street, Rope Walk and Spring Way, all of which are closed to traffic for the race. Major roads crossed: Ferry Road and High Street. The finish is in Foundry Yard.

Course dimensions
The course uses wide carriageways throughout. Dyer Street offers 9 m kerb to kerb, Bell Street about 16 m and Spring Way about 10 m, with footways of a further 3 m on each side. The field assembles on Dyer Street, and the finish is in Foundry Yard, an open paved area of around one and a half hectares.

Support
Entrants collect numbers from the top of Dyer Street from one hour before the start. Timing is by chip, with mats at the start and finish. Results are posted on the Harbour Harriers website the same day.

attachments.name: traffic_plan.txt
attachments.text:
Traffic arrangements for the Harbour Harriers City Race 7K, Saturday 8 May 2027

From Ruth Abernathy, Event Coordinator, Harbour Harriers Athletic Club

We have tried to think through what happens on the roads on race day. The race is a 7K, it starts at 09:00, and it goes through the Kingsway Gardens area. See the attached correspondence from the police for the escort.

Closing the roads
We need the following closures, and Northline Barriers will put out the barriers and signs for us. Dyer Street from Quay Street to Orchard Road, 07:45 until 11:00. Tanner Street from Albion Road to Quay Street, 07:45 until 11:00. Bell Street from Orchard Road to Castle Way, 07:45 until 11:00. Rope Walk from Quay Street to Linden Avenue, 07:45 until 11:00. Spring Way from Quay Street to Linden Avenue, 07:45 until 11:00.

Crossings
Our marshals are experienced and they know the area, so they will keep a good eye out at the busier junctions and let runners know when it's clear. We'll move people around on the day depending on how busy things look.

Getting around the closures
We've worked out the way round for drivers and Northline Barriers will sign it. Traffic off Dyer Street goes via Tram Street and Victoria Road, signed from Linden Avenue. Traffic off Tanner Street goes via Station Road and Church Road, signed from Quay Street. Traffic off Bell Street goes via Prince Street and Regent Road, signed from Foundry Street. Traffic off Rope Walk goes via Cross Avenue and Dock Road, signed from Linden Avenue. Traffic off Spring Way goes via Queen's Road and Station Road, signed from Quay Street.

Emergency vehicles
I've no doubt an ambulance or a fire engine would get through if one were needed. Everybody on our team knows to get out of the way and to help in any way they can, and we'll be sure to mention the race to the fire station.

Volunteers get a short note about the day in race week, with their start time, and are asked to find a replacement if they cannot make it. Most of them have done this before and know the area well.

Letting people know
We put the race on our Facebook page and in the club newsletter, and the local paper usually gives us a mention.

Afterwards
Our sweep vehicle follows the last runner, and each closure comes off in turn once it has passed and the road is clear. Everything will be open again by 11:00.
